title: Release sprint anchor & incident comms template
content:
Purpose and intended audience:
This is a compact, day-of release sprint anchor combined with a lightweight incident communications template. Intended for release owners, on-call SRE, deployment leads, and PG/PM partners. Use it for quick reference during day-of launches and as the basis for post-launch notes.

High-level goals for the sprint day:
- Keep the launch within the agreed telemetry windows (error budget and latency SLOs)
- Ensure 1-minute ack for Sev1 alerts, 5-minute for Sev2
- Preserve customer-facing experience: degrade gracefully if components fail
- Capture decisions and times to aid retrospective and billing reconciliation

Quick pre-launch checklist (T-minus 24h to 1h):
- [ ] Final smoke test checklist reviewed and signed by QA (ticket: RELEASE-452)
- [ ] Canary cohort size defined and set in routing policy (default: 3% user traffic)
- [ ] Throttle and safety lanes configured in deployment controller (safety-lane: 0.6 concurrency)
- [ ] Rollback procedure and verified rollback image available in artifact registry
- [ ] Ops Slack channel created: #release-YYYYMMDD-anchor (invite: eng-release, sres, product-owner)
- [ ] Pager duty rotation confirmed for the launch window
- [ ] Observability dashboards pinned: latency-5m, errors-1m, token-cost-avg, model-kvcache-hit
- [ ] Synthetic workload run and results attached to release ticket

Day-of sprint timeline (anchor cadence):
- -60m: final preflight — confirm migration gates, schema locks, config flags
- -30m: team stand by — shift roster posted, console owners assigned
- 0m: start rollout — open canary, set routing policy to canary cohort
- +5m: canary health check — golden signals reviewed, depending on pass expand to 10%
- +30m: steady expand to target percentage (per rollout plan) with 10–15m observation windows
- +2h: full route or follow staged policy; if any signal >= threshold, execute safety-lane
- +4h: post-launch telemetry snapshot and quick notes; if stable, update status to stable in ticket

Signals and thresholds (golden signals):
- Error rate: >0.5% increase over baseline for 5m -> alert P1
- 95th percentile latency: >x ms (model dependent) -> alert P2
- Model rejection/invalid response: any production error count >10 in 15m -> investigate
- Token cost spike: >20% change over rolling day baseline -> investigate for runaway prompts

Annotated incident comms template (use for Slack/email updates)
- Subject / Slack header: [RELEASE] <component> — <short status> — <UTC HH:MM>
- Opening line: Brief one-liner: what happened, who owns it, current state
  Example: "[RELEASE] Hosted API routing — degraded responses — 2026-03-21 15:12 UTC. Owning: Asha P. Impacted: 2% of requests; team: eng-sre / serving-runtime."
- Impact summary: affected customers, percentage of traffic, user-visible symptoms
- Current mitigation: what we did (toggle flag, redirected traffic, scaled pool)
- Next action plan & ETA: next steps and who is assigned with timeboxes
- Public-facing notes (for CS): canned blurb for status page/CS teams
  Example: "Experiencing elevated latencies for a subset of requests. Working on mitigation. No data loss reported. Updates every 15 minutes."
- Timeline log (fill in during incident):
  - 15:12 UTC — alert triggered: increased 5m error rate
  - 15:14 UTC — on-call ack, reroute initiated to fallback model variant
  - 15:18 UTC — partial mitigation: canary reduced to 0.5% traffic
  - 15:40 UTC — follow-up: latencies returning but still above threshold

Rollback matrix (decision points and triggers):
- Soft rollback (reduce cohort/disable feature flag): when error rate >0.5% for 10m AND latency degraded by 25%
- Hard rollback (full revert to previous image): when user-visible degradation persists after 30m with no improvement OR safety-lane manual trigger
- Post-rollback steps: capture logs, attach tracer snapshots, run smoke tests from the previous stable image, update all stakeholders

Notes about communications frequency and cadence:
- For degradations with customer impact: post updates every 15 minutes until mitigated
- For minor noisy alerts with no user impact: short Slack note and hourly updates
- After event: one consolidated summary in ticket and postmortem template filled within 72 hours

Release notes draft (to be dropped into CHANGELOG / release ticket):
- Release headline: "2026-03-21: routing policy refinement + kvcache stability patches"
- What changed (short bullets):
  - Adjusted canary routing to support vertical splits -> lower cold-start P99 for small requests
  - KV cache eviction fix to address memory fragmenting in long-lived sessions
  - Added telemetry tag to token billing events for better cost attribution
- Known issues: "Under certain burst patterns, metric backends show spurious spikes — harmless but noisy. Traces attached."
- Rollout plan summary: staged rollout starting at 3% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 15m observation windows

Post-release retro anchor (template points to capture):
- Successes (what went well): short bullets
- Pain points (what blocked): short bullets with owners for remediation
- Followups (tickets created): list tickets and owners, due dates
- RCA owner and draft ETA for postmortem: usually within 5 business days

Quick decision heuristics (cheat sheet for owners):
- If both error rate and latency spike -> prioritise rollback over scaling if rollback is sub-5m
- If spike correlates with a specific region, prefer region-based routing fallback before global rollback
- If cost spike without user-visible impact, pause non-critical background jobs and throttle burst windows

Open questions & TODOs (notes-to-self / follow-up list):
- TODO: Add canned CS status page blurb variants for multi-region incidents (Lina)
- TODO: Validate rollback image push verification and signing (Marco)
- Question: should we make the default canary cohort 1% for latency-sensitive models?
- Investigate: noise in metric pipeline described in 'Known issues' bullet — root cause tracked in RELEASE-452

Appendix: useful links and commands
- Infra deploy CLI: gh infra deploy --release RELEASE-452 --staged
- Quick toggle for safety lane: /ops toggle-safety --release RELEASE-452 --state on
- Dashboards: https://telemetry.redwood.com/dashboards/latency-5m
- Postmortem template: confluence:redwood-postmortem-template

Author notes (scratchpad):
- Keep this doc as the minimum viable anchor for small/medium rollouts; for larger launches expand the guardrails and cross-functional comms cadence to 30-minute public updates and a war-room phone bridge.
- If we start seeing repeated regressions from model quantization changes, add an explicit canary variant that uses previous quantization profile for rapid fallback.

End of document.
